text: Schroedinger argued that living systems maintain their improbable internal order by feeding on ___, the low-entropy, energy-rich material they take in, while expelling high-entropy material, so that the second law of thermodynamics is never violated.
explanation: The answer is 'negentropy' (negative entropy). A living system imports low-entropy, ordered material and exports high-entropy material, locally maintaining order while increasing the total entropy of the universe. This is why maintaining life requires continual sensing and work, and why no second-law violation occurs.
